verdict.reasoning: The patient describes a sudden-onset left-sided headache beginning this morning about four hours prior: “So it started in the morning… It came like kind of suddenly… the headache started like four… four hours ago… left side of the head, exactly.”
Pain intensity is 5–6/10 and compared to prior kidney stone pain rated as 10: “Well, I had the kidney stone, so let’s say that that’s 10 I have now maybe five. Well, six.”
Visual disturbance with blurred vision and zigzag lines is reported: “My vision is quite blurred… Like some zigzag lines kind of.”
She reports intolerance to screens, which is consistent with photophobia: “I cannot stand screens.”

She reports dizziness that worsens with movement/standing: “I feel like dizzy… when I move… if I leave bed I start to feel like even worse if I move. So I just want to have my head like really not moving.”
She reports nausea with two vomiting episodes and ongoing nausea: “I vomit twice… As soon as the headache started, I also vomited… and I still feel nausea. I’m about to vomit very soon, I think.”

She took paracetamol about three hours before with no effect: “I tried paracetamol but didn’t work… the headache started like four… four hours ago. So I would say like maybe three hours ago because I couldn’t stand it.”
She denies prior similar headaches: “Have you ever had a headache like this in the past?” / “Well, not really because it’s a first. Yeah, like this? No, definitely it’s something new.”
No focal weakness or gait disturbance reported: “Have you noticed any weakness in your arms or legs?” / “No… No.” and “when you’re walking… are you walking a bit funny?” / “Not really.”
History of kidney stones is mentioned: “You’ve mentioned in the past you’ve had kidney stones.”
She takes no regular medications: “Do you take any regular medications?” / “No.”
She took paracetamol for this episode: “Have you tried any painkillers for this already?” / “Yeah, I tried paracetamol but didn’t work.”
No drug allergies reported: “Are you allergic to any medications?” / “Not that I’m aware. Yeah, not that I’m aware.”
Mother has migraines: “My mother has migraines.”
Mother has hypothyroidism: “And also, I have hypothyroidism in the family… She also has hypothyroidism.”
She doubts she is pregnant: “Is there any chance you could be pregnant?” / “I really doubt it.”

Doctor assesses probable migraine with unilateral pain, visual symptoms, nausea/vomiting, first presentation: “So it sounds like what you’re suffering from is what’s known as a migraine… it’s on one side of the head… you’ve got blurry vision… with the nausea and vomiting… very typical of a migraine.” She also says she’s never had this before.

Patient expresses concern about tumor or stroke, and no focal neuro symptoms are reported: “this can be some kind of brain tumor or something… Or maybe a stroke.” and later doctor summarizes “you’ve got no neurological symptoms. You’re walking fine.”
Ibuprofen OTC is recommended: “I would recommend in the time between now and when we can see you take some medications, maybe something like ibuprofen.”
Antiemetic from pharmacy is suggested: “So there’s lots of medication treatments. So they can be ibuprofen with an anti sickness which you can get from the pharmacy.”
Sugary carbonated drink like Coke is suggested: “and also to drink a sugary carbonated drink, something like coke.”
Specific migraine preparation (Migraleve) is to be considered: “Then we can go up the treatment ladder. You can get specific migraleve medication.”

A same-day review/neurological exam is to be arranged, with option to cancel if better: “we would want to see you as soon as possible to do like a full neurological exam… we could see you today at some point… if… you feel much better… you can cancel it.”

She is advised to seek further help if problems continue or worsen: “Any further problems between now and your appointment, please do let us know.” This implies urgent review if no improvement or worsening.
